title: Shared and class-specific heterogeneity cannot be told apart below about 40 studies per class
question: How many studies per class are needed before model comparison reliably distinguishes a shared between-study variance from class-specific ones?
design: Two classes of 2 to 40 studies each with between-study variance ratio 1, 2 or 5; shared and separate REML fits compared by AIC, BIC and a likelihood-ratio test. 21 cells, 2000 replicates each.
answer: No. Even with a fivefold difference in between-study variance, AIC chose class-specific variances in only 18% of networks with five studies per class, 40% with twelve and 79% with forty. Balanced selection accuracy reached 0.8 only at 40 studies per class and only for AIC; BIC and a likelihood-ratio test did not within 40. At the network sizes population-adjusted analyses use, the heterogeneity structure cannot be chosen from the data, so the shared default is untested rather than supported.
findings: Twofold variance ratio: separate structure chosen in at most 27% of networks by any criterion up to 40 studies per class.
AIC false-positive rate rose from 0.6% (2 studies per class) to 15% (40).
BIC with two studies per class chose separate variances under the null in 12% because its penalty log(2m-2) is below 2.
not_answered: Two classes, contrast-level data, frequentist criteria; no Bayesian model comparison, informative priors, ML-NMR or class-specific treatment SD. Peer review has not been done.
estimand: Probability of selecting the true heterogeneity structure
